svg.title: How a passage's category chooses its translation skill
svg.desc: Once, on the source, a model reads a passage whole and names its category, one of twelve families; outside evidence such as study notes reaches this step only. Code selects a skill from the category or holds at the general plan. The skill sets five steps of the run for one passage: what the drafter is told, what the alignment must account for, which checks run, what sends a draft back and how often, and how the best pass is chosen. The run records the skill and why. A grid shows what the general plan and the records, law, poetry and argument skills each change at those five steps, and whether each is as today, measured to work, built but off, or proposed.
svg.text: How a passage's category chooses its translation skill
A genealogy, a law, a poem and an argument fail in different ways. The category of a passage chooses a skill, and the skill sets five steps of the run.
ONCE, ON THE SOURCE: THE SAME FOR EVERY LANGUAGE
the skill sets these five steps

g.text: what sends it back, how often
how the best pass is chosen

svg.text: all other kinds, or a hold
the first draft wins a tie
No check of its own yet
built, and measured to catch planted errors
built and tested: no gain shown yet, so it is off
A wrong category must cost little: a skill adds care for one kind of text and takes away nothing the general plan requires. A hold changes nothing.
